explanation: Fires on a personal pronoun (mostly possessive his/her/their/my/your, also he/they/I/you) that opens a noun phrase naming a role or relationship to someone already mentioned, especially right after a copula or in a relative clause: 'X is [her] coach', 'was [their] third base coach', 'the person [I] admire', 'the company [they] work for'. Generic pronouns not in such a predicative/relational slot give weak activation; other tokens give almost none.

Fires on 'the' (and sometimes the verb itself) right after verbs of change like improve, enhance, lower, reduce or increase in outcome or efficiency talk ('improving conversion rates and [the] chances', 'enhance [the] efficiency'). It fires more weakly on sentence-final periods and opening 'The' in medical or statistical abstracts that report results ('survival', 'median', '5-year'). It also fires a little on other result-summary tokens.

Fires on a middle or final subword piece that completes a long multi-token identifier or rare word, such as an API/class name in code (UIImagePickerController, android.content[.Intent], TextInputType, stdbool, UnknownHostException) or a rare word or proper name split into pieces (Bing[ham]ton, pilgr-ims, babys[itters], McCorm-ack, psychiat-rists). Common whole words give little activation.

Fires on joining punctuation inside a word or identifier: hyphens in compounds (now-destroyed, super-elite, re-imagined, US-Präsidenten), hyphens and slashes in URL slugs or module paths, French elision apostrophes (l'), the Japanese middle dot, '+' in URLs, and ObjC ' *)'. It also fires on garbled Devanagari byte tokens. Spaces, parentheses and other code punctuation give moderate to weak activation.

A mixture. It fires strongly on 'of' inside organization names (Society of, School of, National Association of), on 'were' after plural subjects in research abstracts, on 'personal' in 'personal computer/digital assistant', and on assorted pieces of names and words (Sal-ido, Mult-ilateral, -old). No single context links these.

Fires in CSS and similar key-value code on the colon after a property name, or on the space before its value (height: 0px, width:, left: 0, min-width:). It fires more weakly on nearby syntax tokens in code and config (=, '(', '>&', '":', ' Name', ' ='). Prose gives almost nothing.

Fires on tokens inside ALL-CAPS text, especially the second or later piece of an uppercase word or the next word in an all-caps headline, name or legal caption (BIRMING[HAM], G[IL]BERT, SN[OW], OUT [OF], [HIGH] STRESS, UCP LE[ADER]). Uppercase words in code macros or license text give weaker activation; lowercase text gives none.

Fires on tokens in the title or opening sentence of a programming Q&A question, right after 'Q:', such as 'I [am] trying', 'Here is [my] code', 'works [fine]', '[not] working', 'Say I have'. It fires most strongly at the very start of the question body, and more weakly on later first-person problem narration. Answers and code bodies give little.

Fires on a token that is the near-certain next piece of a stock phrase or boilerplate string: '/android' in the Android xmlns URL, 'assistance' in 'ineffective assistance of counsel', 'Cuts' in Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, 'to' in 'brought to you by', 'editor' in 'Letter to the editor', 'more' in the Apache license header, 'IZATION' in Immigration and Naturalization. Less formulaic text gives weak activation.

A mixture: SVG path-data letters, digits in math or chemistry text, code indentation and closing brackets, garbled Devanagari bytes, and assorted nouns after a determiner ('the offensive [message]', 'this [ceramic] material', 'ideal [conditions]'). No common thread is visible.

Fires on the later token(s) that complete a well-known multi-token proper name, acronym or technical term: Alcat[raz], receiver [operating] characteristic, cognitive-beh[avior]al, Haemodial[ysis], OS[HA], NMD[A], Historic [Places], Dead [Sea], Phase [III], echocardi[ography]. The first token of the term and ordinary words do not fire.

A mixture: 'attributes' and 'License'/'law' in software boilerplate headers, hyphens inside GUIDs, plus scattered prose tokens ('you're [burning] cash', 'the [family]', 'Is [Perfect] For', 'Cannot [read] property'). There is no clear shared trigger.

Fires on verbs, verb endings and function words in running Spanish or Portuguese prose (como, será, es, foi, tiveram, até, que, -u/-i past-tense endings). It fires more weakly on 'de'/'del' inside Spanish or Portuguese institution names in otherwise English text. English text gives almost nothing.

Fires at a structural boundary at the start of a line where a block ends or a new section begins: the end of a license header (CDDL HEADER END, '=====' separator lines), indentation before closing braces or 'end', 'End Sub', '</head>', the 'A:' that opens an answer, and section numerals like 'I.'. Ordinary mid-sentence tokens give weak activation.

Loosely fires at the first token of a new sentence or clause that continues the previous one, often a back-referring determiner ('This one is', 'These frames', 'another', 'such a') or a conjunction ('and', 'if'). Many top examples are just ordinary words ('police', 'hit', 'crossed', 'cover'), so the pattern is weak and mixed.

Fires on the second piece of a multi-token name or identifier: 'Janeiro' after 'Rio de', 'ertest' in supertest, 'ful' in restful, '.php' in file names, surname pieces (New-bould, Lack-ey, Martin after Trayvon). It also fires on the '(' newline after a Go 'import' following a generated-code header. Ordinary prose gives weak activation.

Fires on tokens in object-oriented class or interface declarations: protocol and superclass names in the header (UIViewControllerAnimated, NSCopying), '@interface', '__construct', 'interface', 'namespace', '@property', and the indentation before the first member inside a class body. Code outside declaration headers and prose give little.

A mixture: 'Message' in email '-----Original Message-----', subword pieces of names and words in several languages (S[GB]D, aspir[in], Lozan Antlaş[ması], Kaisersl[aut]ern), 'Christ', 'Team Up', 'of' after 'discovery/presence'. There is no single trigger.

Fires mainly on pieces of cytokine and growth-factor names in biomedical text (chem[ok]ine, V[EG]F, SC[F], bFG[F], growth [factor]) and on research-grant or award wording (career [development], NSF CARE[ER], This [project] was funded, claims the benefit). It also fires on visa and immigration terms (H-1B, visa, Deferred Action). Several loosely linked themes.

Fires on a function word (the, of, a/an, to) in a formal encyclopedic or legal sentence that places the subject in a larger category, place or legal frame: 'Title 29 of [the] Code', 'in [the] genus', 'under [the] laws of', 'Coast [of] Vietnam', 'is [an] autosomal', 'licensed under [the] Apache License'. The same words in casual text fire weakly.
